outcome: Metrics now uses one extensible read-only scientific-state snapshot
owner_impact: The former hard-coded Metrics whitelist is replaced by a single scientific snapshot boundary. Metrics can measure actual backend kinematics, applied actions, run-local agent identity, authored per-agent private scientific state, Experiment configuration, named references and the active environment without granting mutation or host access. Existing Metrics source remains compatible, and future simulator-owned scientific state must declare its Metrics projection instead of adding another one-off field.

next.text: Next is #526 — population identity and opt-in local recognition. It will add stable population/group identity plus separately enabled local recognition, using the scientific snapshot introduced here for global measurement. #526 has not started.

technical_evidence: Kernel measurement now uses vlab.scientific-snapshot/0.1 instead of raw AgentPhysicalState plus ad-hoc reference arguments.
Planar velocity and angular velocity are retained from the actual physics integration step rather than reconstructed from post-step heading or controller commands.
Metrics static snapshot fields/functions are derived from implemented capability bindings; Experiment-specific configuration, reference and private-state projections are added at compile time.
Browser and MCP Metrics compilers remain mirrored and existing Active Elastic Metrics remain source-compatible.
The read-only boundary excludes RNG engine internals, neighbour-index internals, host state, transport buffers and mutation APIs.
